anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address pin A0 (pin 1) is tied to +3.3V, while A1-A5 are tied to GND, setting the I2C address to 0x41 as noted on the schematic.
anomalies.expected: Per the design specification, the PCA9685PW should have I2C address 0x40, which requires all address pins A0-A5 to be tied to GND.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40
I2C address: 0x41 (FCC Peripherals sheet, under PWM Driver)

anomalies.impact: The PWM driver will respond at I2C address 0x41 instead of 0x40, so software expecting 0x40 will fail to communicate with the servo driver.

anomalies.observed: CH330 U11 TXD (pin 5) connects to UART1_TX_FCC (MCU TX) and RXD (pin 6) connects to UART1_RX_FCC (MCU RX). U12 similarly connects TXD to UART3_TX_NAVC and RXD to UART3_RX_NAVC.
anomalies.expected: Standard USB-UART bridge wiring requires the bridge's TXD to connect to the MCU's RX and the bridge's RXD to the MCU's TX, i.e. TXD to UART1_RX_FCC/UART3_RX_NAVC and RXD to UART1_TX_FCC/UART3_TX_NAVC.

evidence.quote: U11 otter_CH330: pin 5 (TXD) wired to UART1_TX_FCC; pin 6 (RXD) wired to UART1_RX_FCC. U12: pin 5 to UART3_TX_NAVC, pin 6 to UART3_RX_NAVC (Connections sheet).

anomalies.impact: The USB-UART bridges will not communicate with the MCUs because the TX and RX lines are not crossed, preventing USB programming/debug over these interfaces.

parsed.summary: Two anomalies were found: the PCA9685 PWM driver is strapped for I2C address 0x41 instead of the specified 0x40, and both CH330 USB-UART bridges have their TXD/RXD lines connected straight through rather than crossed.
